answer: Because the juniper index resolves every citation against the copper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pigment audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 127 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 127 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 2222 identities would post 2426 proofs and burn roughly 56 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
